messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] Error with saalfeld xform
messages.body_plain:
Dear Ansh, thanks for your interest in nat and sorry you’ve run into trouble here. Could you run

nat.h5reg::dr_h5reg()

and report what it says? For good measure you could also run

sessioninfo::session_info()

All the best,

Greg.

> On 1 Feb 2021, at 19:55, Ansh Gandhi <haduke...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> ﻿Hey all,
>
> I am trying to transform a neuron that I have retrieved from hemibrain to FAFB space, then plot it 3-dimensionally using this code:
> library(natverse); library(nat.jrcbrains);
> LHAV1a1.hemibrain = neuprint_read_neurons("LHAV1a1");
> LHAV1a1.hemibrain.fafb = xform_brain(LHAV1a1.hemibrain*8/1000, reference= "FAFB14", sample="JRCFIB2018F", via=JRC2018F);
> plot3d(LHAV1a1.hemibrain.fafb, lwd=2); plot3d(FAFB);
>
> However, when running, the code never gets past the xform_brain command and throws this error consistently:
> Transforming neurons using the sequence: JRCFIB2018F->JRC2018F->FAFB14um->FAFB14
> Error in saalfeld_xform(points, reg, inverse = !swapped, ...) :
>   Error running saalfeld xform!
>
> As a result, only the FAFB space is plotted without the transformed neuron. I am relatively new to this, so this may be a simple fix, but I can't seem to figure it out.
>
> Any and all help would be very much appreciated!
>
> Sincerely,
> Ansh Gandhi
>
> --

messages.body_plain:
Hi Dr. Jefferis,

Thanks for the prompt reply! I actually managed to solve the error by running that first command. It threw a few errors, and I realized that my computer did not have a JDK set up on it due to the fact that it is relatively new. I set up the latest Oracle JDK and set my PATH variables, and the registration worked like it was supposed to! This is why I deleted the post.

Thank you for the help!

Sincerely,

Ansh Gandhi

messages.body_plain:
Dear Greg,

I also came across this issue, please let me know if a solution is underway. Also, I am open to other suggestions you might have as to how to show a neuron obtained from natverse overlaid onto an nc82 template brain.

Sincerely,

Jon

On Tuesday, January 12, 2021 at 7:59:36 PM UTC-5 jeff...@gmail.com wrote:
> Dear Rory,
>
> That means that your image dimensions are too large for the current code:
>
> 2^31
> [1] 2147483648
>
> i.e. ~2GB
>
> > (2^31)^(1/3)
> [1] 1290.159
>
> So the limit is about 1290 x 1290 x 1290 or the same product with a different side ratio. I personally have not had to deal with images of this size in R. My first suggestion is to consider slightly increasing your voxel size. If that's not an option then the code needs to be modified. This is the place:
>
> https://github.com/natverse/nat/blob/4d85cc7a2ea66cecd0576c0ff2fe96be722a5341/R/nrrd-io.R#L459-L461
>
> I don't have time to do this just now, but if you want to try and have a go by cloning the nat repo, I think something like the below should work (untested). I'd also recommend making a GitHub issue
>
> https://github.com/natverse/nat/issues
>
> All the best,
>
> Greg.
>
> # add a new function
>
> #' Split slices of an image into chunks based on maximum integer index size
> #'
> #' @details in R linear indices into arrays can only be 2^31 long (32 bit int).
> #'   This means that \code{writeBin} can only write this many pixels in one go.
> #'   Therefore to write bigger pixel arrays, you must split the images into chunks
> #'   for writing. NB this function currently only works for 3D arrays.
> #'
> #' @param x An array containing image data
> #' @param max_chunk_size (default is max for writeBin)
> #'
> #' @return a vector of length the number of slices, giving the chunk index (1:nchunks)
> #'   for each slice.
> make_image_chunks <- function(x, max_chunk_size=2^31-1) {
>   lastdim=length(dim(x))
>   # FIXME handle arrays that are not 3D
>   stopifnot(lastdim==3)
>   nslices=dim(x)[lastdim]
>   slice_size=prod(dim(x)[-lastdim])
>   if(slice_size>max_chunk_size)
>     stop("write.nrrd cannot write data with slices with > 2^31 pixels")
>   slices_per_chunk=1 + (max_chunk_size %/% slice_size)
>   chunk_size=slices_per_chunk * slice_size
>   nchunks=1 + nslices %/% slices_per_chunk
>   #
>   chunks=rep(seq_len(nchunks), rep(slices_per_chunk, nchunks))[seq_len(nslices)]
>   chunks
> }
>
> # edit these lines:
> # https://github.com/natverse/nat/blob/4d85cc7a2ea66cecd0576c0ff2fe96be722a5341/R/nrrd-io.R#L459-L461
>
> fc=ifelse(enc=="gzip", gzfile, base::file)(file, open=fmode)
> if(length(x)>=2^31 && max(chunks <- make_image_chunks(x))>1) {
>   # too big, must chunk
>   for(i in seq_len(max(chunks))) {
>     writeBin(as.vector(x[, , chunks == i], mode = dmode),
>              fc,
>              size = dtypesize,
>              endian = endian)
>   }
> } else {
>   # write in one go
>   writeBin(as.vector(x, mode=dmode), fc, size=dtypesize, endian=endian)
> }
> close(fc)
>
>
> > On 12 Jan 2021, at 16:23, Rory Beresford <rory.be...@research.fchampalimaud.org> wrote:
> >
> > Hello all,
> >
> > i've been having some issues with the write.im3d function. I have read neurons into R and transformed them to various brain registrations. I'm now looking to convert these to .nrrd files, but have been getting an unexpected error which I haven't been able to solve:
> >
> > neuron <- neuprint_read_neurons(5813046951, heal = TRUE, heal.threshold = 1e9, connectors=FALSE)
> > neuron.JRC2018U <- xform_brain(neuron*8/1000, reference=JRC2018U, sample="JRCFIB2018F")
> > im <- as.im3d(xyzmatrix(neuron.JRC2018U), JRC2018U)
> > write.im3d(im, "5813011145.nrrd")
> >
> > with this code, I get the error message:
> > Error in writeBin(as.vector(x, mode = dmode), fc, size = dtypesize, endian = endian) :
> >   only 2^31-1 bytes can be written in a single writeBin() call
> >
> > This error occurs while testing a number of other neurons. I've also tried using write.nrrd but I still get the error.
> >
> > Does anyone have any ideas on what might be causing the error and how to work around it? Would be very grateful for the help.
> >
> > Thanks,
> > Rory
> >
> >
> >
> > --
> > You received this message because you are subscribed to the Google Groups "nat-user" group.
> > To unsubscribe from this group and stop receiving emails from it, send an email to nat-user+u...@googlegroups.com.
> > To view this discussion on the web, visit https://groups.google.com/d/msgid/nat-user/c56d8366-68c7-4f42-828a-09285c70e91dn%40googlegroups.com <https://groups.google.com/d/msgid/nat-user/c56d8366-68c7-4f42-828a-09285c70e91dn%40googlegroups.com?utm_medium=email&utm_source=footer>.
>

messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] Issue with write.im3d
messages.body_plain:
Dear Jon,

If you fancy trying your hand at coding, I have posted most of the solution below.

That said, if your goal is to co-display neurons and volume data, there may be better solutions

1. You can use simple neurite tracer to display SWC files in Fiji in slice or 3d view.

2. You can use https://github.com/takashi310/VVD_Viewer (a fork of fluorender) to generate high quality volumetric rendering in conjunction with an SWC

Other options include

* Vaa3D
* Amira (commercial, but we've used this a lot in the past. This package might be helpful https://github.com/jefferis/nat.amira)
* Paraview (if you write your neuron to VTK format with write.neurons(nl, format='vtk'))

Best,

Greg.

> > >
> > > All the best,
> > >
> > > Greg.
> > >
> > > # add a new function
> > >
> > > #' Split slices of an image into chunks based on maximum integer index size
> > > #'
> > > #' @details in R linear indices into arrays can only be 2^31 long (32 bit int).
> > > #'   This means that \code{writeBin} can only write this many pixels in one go.
> > > #'   Therefore to write bigger pixel arrays, you must split the images into chunks
> > > #'   for writing. NB this function currently only works for 3D arrays.
> > > #'
> > > #' @param x An array containing image data
> > > #' @param max_chunk_size (default is max for writeBin)
> > > #'
> > > #' @return a vector of length the number of slices, giving the chunk index (1:nchunks)
> > > #'   for each slice.
> > > make_image_chunks <- function(x, max_chunk_size=2^31-1) {
> > >   lastdim=length(dim(x))
> > >   # FIXME handle arrays that are not 3D
> > >   stopifnot(lastdim==3)
> > >   nslices=dim(x)[lastdim]
> > >   slice_size=prod(dim(x)[-lastdim])
> > >   if(slice_size>max_chunk_size)
> > >     stop("write.nrrd cannot write data with slices with > 2^31 pixels")
> > >   slices_per_chunk=1 + (max_chunk_size %/% slice_size)
> > >   chunk_size=slices_per_chunk * slice_size
> > >   nchunks=1 + nslices %/% slices_per_chunk
> > >   #
> > >   chunks=rep(seq_len(nchunks), rep(slices_per_chunk, nchunks))[seq_len(nslices)]
> > >   chunks
> > > }
> > >
> > > # edit these lines:
> > > # https://github.com/natverse/nat/blob/4d85cc7a2ea66cecd0576c0ff2fe96be722a5341/R/nrrd-io.R#L459-L461
> > >
> > > fc=ifelse(enc=="gzip", gzfile, base::file)(file, open=fmode)

> > >   # too big, must chunk

> > >              endian = endian)
> > >   }
> > > } else {
> > >   # write in one go

> > > }
> > > close(fc)

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

This one is hard to pin down where the change has occurred but previously when loading neurons from catmaid, aligning and saving to SWC the soma point was labelled with the appropriate SWC type.

It's worth noting previously we had to also scale the radius from nm->um manually this seems to now be handled automatically - so thanks to whoever fixed that.

However now the soma point is marked with a 0 type (undefined) as most of all the other nodes instead of 1 (soma) as had previously been the case.

Has something changed in how soma points are interpreted or should I be looking for changes in the catmaid API?

Any help you can give would be appreciated, Thanks,

Rob Court

Greg.
